classification.difficultyReason: Translate unions, intersections and complements into shaded regions, then compare both sides of each statement on the supplied two-set diagram.

content.prompt: Consider the following statements. Determine whether they are true or false by shading the relevant areas on two-way Venn diagrams.

spec.sourceRegion: Problem 1, shared diagram between the direction and the three statements
spec.description: Unshaded universal rectangle with two horizontally overlapping circles. A is in the left-only region and B is in the right-only region.
spec.mathematics: Two intersecting sets with two exclusive regions, a shared region and an exterior region.

answer.worked: Shade only the overlap for $A\cap B$. Shade the two exclusive regions and the area outside both circles for $\bar A\cup\bar B$. The shaded regions differ, so the statement is false.

spec.sourceRegion: Problem 1(a), using the shared two-set scaffold
spec.description: Paired diagrams compare the two expressions in source order.
spec.mathematics: Left shades the intersection. Right shades the complement of the intersection.

answer.worked: Shade both circles, including their overlap, for $A\cup B$. For $\bar A\cup\bar B$, shade the two exclusive regions and the area outside both circles. The overlap belongs only to the left-hand side, and the exterior belongs only to the right-hand side.

spec.sourceRegion: Problem 1(b), using the shared two-set scaffold
spec.description: Paired diagrams compare the two expressions in source order.
spec.mathematics: Left shades the union. Right shades the two exclusive regions and the exterior.

answer.worked: For $\bar A\cup\bar B$, shade every region outside at least one circle. For $\overline{(A\cap B)}$, shade everything outside the overlap. Both expressions shade the same three regions, so the statement is true.

spec.sourceRegion: Problem 1(c), using the shared two-set scaffold
spec.description: Paired diagrams show identical shading for the two expressions.
spec.mathematics: Both diagrams shade all regions except the intersection.
